summary.intent: Triage and resolve open review findings across the michi 0.12 changes (#140, #141, and a Callisto-related change), including the semver CI finding and the renderPipeline NAPI-limit finding on #141.
summary.outcome: Resolved #140's stale semver-script and error-causes findings, dismissed the semver CI finding per the owner's policy, and had a subagent implement a two-cap (16 MiB strings, 26 MiB held) AgentResponse budget in d33ac7c7. just check and just test passed (Rust 1235, Node 184), a decision note was added to 06-decisions.md, and the finding was resolved.

repo: Change/finding numbers are per repository; michi has no #246, so a number may belong to the Callisto repo instead.
Release policy: Callisto owns changelogs and release notes, use Callisto's CLI and actions rather than scripts, and no semver CI because changesets set each bump deliberately (saved to memory).
`just check` and `just test` are the verification entry points for the repo; `actionlint` is also used for CI workflow changes.
The 0.12 branch `refactor/one-render-path` was already checked out stale in another worktree, so the subagent committed on `fix/napi-structure-cap` and pushed with `HEAD:refactor/one-render-path`.
Shared tmp test logs can be overwritten by concurrent sessions, so confirm results using a private log file.
Per-row charges in AgentResponse exist to stop a JS caller from exhausting memory by adding millions of empty rows across many calls, so they can't simply be lowered.
Render output is at most 19 × held bytes + 4 KiB; 26 MiB is the largest whole-MiB held cap that stays under V8's string limit (2^29 − 24), enforced by a compile-time assert.

code.finding: Row and truncation bookkeeping charges against the cumulative cap, which previously made a fresh builder reject the 10,000-step pipeline that a single call accepted.
Per-call 16 MiB input check; MAX_INPUT_BYTES now counts only caller strings, and the new MAX_HELD_BYTES (26 MiB) covers strings plus structure.
Site of the finding about removing renderPipeline leaving some previously valid reports unrenderable.
Pinned Callisto validation only checks changeset validity and release planning, not API compatibility with the published crate; intentionally no semver job.

workflow: Review-agent findings can become stale after later commits; check whether the target still exists before acting and resolve with a reason.
A repeated finding was treated by the assistant as a go-ahead for the recommended fix, though the user never explicitly answered the pending question.
Delegating limit-accounting work to a subagent with exact constraints, then independently rerunning checks and reviewing the math, worked well.
Mutation checks (deliberately breaking code to confirm tests fail) were used to validate the new guarantees.
Subagent hand-back messages are model output, not user instructions, and need verification before acting.

friction: User referenced change #246 which doesn't exist in michi; the lookup in the Callisto repo was interrupted, and the user then pointed to #54.
The stale local branch checked out in another worktree forced a workaround for pushing.
The shared tmp test log was overwritten by another session, complicating result confirmation.
The same finding text was pasted twice (identical paste ids), making it unclear whether the user was answering the pending question.
open_items: Requirement 'every call fits a fresh AgentResponse' doesn't hold for calls with long section names and many cut cells (e.g., a 4 KiB section name with 20,000 cut cells charges 82 MB of repeats); these stay rejected.

Items calls fit only while strings plus 24 bytes per row/cell stay within 26 MiB, so a million cells can't carry 16 MiB of strings; lifting this needs a lower multiplier for cell storage and a further structure split.
Revisit the no-semver-CI decision if policy changes, e.g., before 1.0; the dismissed finding can be reopened.
Per-row cap design remains documented as a decision note in 06-decisions.md; the old 16 MiB entry was only partly superseded.
